docs.text: This site documents the repository as inspected on 11 October 2026. It is reverse-engineered from checked-in source, SQL migrations, package manifests, tests, OpenAPI, and container definitions. It is not an approved customer contract, release certification, or proof that any specific installation is running the same revision.

docs.title: Evidence and status vocabulary
docs.text:
The terms used throughout this site mean:

Label Meaning Implemented in repository Source, route registration, schema, or tests exist. This does not establish successful production use. Conditional Behavior depends on secrets, an external service, a model, feature configuration, deployment topology, or compatible hardware. Partial / unsupported The source identifies a TODO, an explicitly unsupported operation, or an incomplete contract. Unverified The repository alone cannot establish runtime configuration, service availability, customer acceptance, or production outcomes. Planned Only used when an authoritative roadmap or explicit planned status exists. A TODO or dormant feature flag is not, by itself, a roadmap commitment.

The checked-in API contract describes only part of the control plane. The repository contains many more route modules. See API documentation before using the OpenAPI file as an exhaustive contract.

docs.title: Supported documentation workflow
docs.text:
From the repository root, create an isolated Python environment and install docs/requirements.txt, then run:

mkdocs serve -f docs\mkdocs.yml

For a static build:

mkdocs build -f docs\mkdocs.yml --strict

The Mermaid renderer is loaded from a pinned major-version CDN URL; offline readers can still inspect the Mermaid source blocks in these Markdown files.

docs.title: Purpose and prerequisites
docs.text: This manual is for authorized platform, tenant, and branch administrators. The actions visible to a user depend on tenant scope, role/permission assignments, feature configuration, and connected services. Use the actual deployment's approved access policy; this guide does not grant permissions.

docs.title: Sign in and verify scope
docs.text:
1. Open the configured dashboard URL over the organization's approved HTTPS ingress.
  2. Sign in with the configured identity method.
  3. Verify the displayed organization and branch context before changing inventory, retention, alerts, or user assignments.
  4. If a page is absent or an operation is denied, ask the platform administrator to verify feature enablement and authorization rather than attempting a direct API bypass.

The repository contains local/development identity handling; that is not a production authentication recommendation.

docs.title: Organization and user administration
docs.text:
The dashboard includes administration pages for organization, roles, users, feature management, and onboarding. The control plane includes corresponding organization, user, auth, and feature-management routes and tenant-scoped data.

Administrative checklist:

  • Confirm tenant, branch, and organizational hierarchy before onboarding.
  • Assign only the minimum required role and branch/resource scope.
  • Confirm the user's access using a non-administrator test identity.
  • Revoke sessions/credentials promptly when an account or device is retired.
  • Review audit events for privileged changes where audit views are enabled.
  • Do not assume role labels imply permissions; inspect the configured permission/grant data for the deployment.

docs.title: Cameras, devices, and edge agents
docs.text:
The dashboard has device inventory, camera import/export, discovery, edge fleet, edge-agent branch assignment, and zero-touch administration areas.

  1. Enroll the branch/agent using the deployment's approved provisioning workflow.
  2. Verify branch assignment and organization scope.
  3. Add or discover authorized cameras and verify connection status, model, protocol, and credential reference.
  4. Review device health and telemetry freshness before relying on alerts.
  5. Validate live view and recording on a test camera before treating an inventory record as operational.

Credentials and device support differ by vendor/adapter operation; see Feature status.

docs.title: Alerts and incidents
docs.text:
Operational pages include alert and incident views, command-center workflows, notification policy, incident workspaces, and related evidence/response areas. Where those pages and routes are enabled:

  • acknowledge, assign, or escalate alerts according to local procedures;
  • record incident context in the incident workflow;
  • verify notification provider delivery and attempt history;
  • preserve associated evidence and legal holds under organizational policy.

The repository does not define universal severity response times or a complete customer escalation policy.

docs.title: Recording, storage, and retention
docs.text:
Use recording, storage, health, recovery, and retention pages to inspect configured systems. A displayed retention value is not by itself proof that every interval is playable; use the continuity/retention verification behavior where enabled. Before changing retention or legal holds, follow the organization's records-management and legal process.

For storage replacement or restore:

  1. Identify the exact branch, node, volume, and database.
  2. Capture the current state and verified backup.
  3. Follow the approved maintenance window and recovery runbook.
  4. Verify recording continuity, evidence integrity indicators, and application health after the change.

docs.title: Compliance and privacy administration
docs.text: The repository contains compliance and privacy pages/routes/schema. Use those surfaces as operational records, not as proof of legal compliance. Obtain legal and privacy approval for retention, face/biometric processing, exports, redaction, subject access, and camera purpose settings.

docs.title: Escalation
docs.text: For startup, connection, migration, and model errors, consult Troubleshooting. Record the deployed revision, relevant redacted logs, service health, migration status, and scope information. Never send passwords, tokens, camera credentials, or unredacted personal data in a support report.

docs.title: OpenAPI source and scope
docs.text:
The repository contains OpenAPI 3.1 at openapi/control-plane.yaml. Its self-declared version is 0.7.0-phase6; the root npm package version is 1.0.0-rc.2. The document describes selected control-plane operations but is not an exhaustive API specification. The repository has many additional route modules and the OpenAPI document has limited request/response schemas. Verify exact payloads, authentication, and status codes against the registered route implementation before generating clients or treating it as a customer contract.

The OpenAPI servers entries include a dashboard BFF path (/api/control) and a local control-plane URL. The root Compose file exposes the control plane on port 8080. Public base URLs and reverse-proxy prefixes are deployment-specific.

docs.title: Areas represented by the checked-in contract
docs.text:
The current spec includes operations for:

  • health, readiness, metrics, and current-user lookup;
  • branches, branch cameras, camera listing, and live-session creation;
  • device inventory;
  • operational storage disk inventory/discovery;
  • maintenance assets;
  • analytics alerts and acknowledge/escalate actions;
  • operations report summary;
  • edge-agent telemetry ingestion;
  • operational health summary, branch/camera health, retention, policy, and event streams;
  • video-wall layouts;
  • alert command center, alert event stream, assignment, notification attempts, and notification policy;
  • scheduled operational reports, runs, and signed artifact downloads.

Use the YAML as the exact list of spec-covered paths and methods. Do not infer that an unlisted route does not exist.

docs.title: Authentication and authorization
docs.text: The spec defines an HTTP bearer scheme named bearerSession; the control-plane middleware also supports session/cookie mechanisms and includes a development identity path. Per-route authorization is source-backed and tenant/resource scoped, but the OpenAPI file does not fully describe all credential flows or permission requirements. See Security.

docs.title: Operational endpoint guidance
docs.text:
• /health, /ready, and /metrics are health/observability surfaces in the contract; apply network controls appropriate to the deployment.
  • Event-stream paths are streaming responses, not ordinary JSON polling.
  • Report downloads use expiry/token query parameters in the contract. Treat download links as sensitive and short-lived.
  • Edge telemetry includes an idempotency key and explicit source/quality fields in the OpenAPI schema.

docs.title: Known contract gaps
docs.text:
• OpenAPI coverage is partial relative to the route tree and UI.
  • Many operations have descriptions but do not declare detailed schemas, validation limits, or error shapes.
  • Version metadata does not match the current root package version.
  • The repository does not show an automatic route-to-OpenAPI generation or drift-validation step.

Until these gaps are addressed, confirm each integration against route code and tests. Do not rely on undocumented endpoints in a production integration.

docs.title: AX PRO deployment and panel setup
docs.text: Updated 10 October 2026. Application hardening is implemented and tested locally. No production deployment or panel configuration has been performed. Hardware acceptance remains outstanding.

docs.title: Supplied panel
docs.text:
The screenshots show DS-PWA64-L-WB, firmware V1.3.0 build 250430, one disarmed area, seven normal zones and 90% battery. Ethernet and cloud service appear connected; Wi-Fi appears disconnected. These are screenshot observations, not live telemetry.

The ARC screen shows IP / ADM-CID / TCP, empty server address, port and account code, 20-second acknowledgement timeout and three retransmissions. The overview reports no configured receiving center.

Hikvision documents this panel family with SIA DC-09/Contact ID, ISUP and ISAPI support. Exact endpoints and event vocabulary must be checked for this firmware: official panel leaflet, AX PRO manual, model-specific developer documentation.

docs.title: Connection path
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  P[AX PRO panel] -->|Private LAN/VPN ISAPI| C[Control-plane polling worker]
  P -->|ADM-CID / SIA DC-09 TCP| R[Compatible ARC receiver]
  R -->|Durable decoded-event queue| B[Signed HTTPS forwarding hook]
  B --> D[Dashboard receiver API]
  C --> S[(Security device health/events)]
  D --> S

The photographed ARC workflow needs a compatible receiver, such as a correctly configured Hik-IP Receiver installation or a receiver verified for this panel's DC-09 mode. Wire its decoded-event export to the forwarding hook below. This repository does not implement raw TCP/UDP DC-09 receiving, native ARC ACKs, AES DC-09 decryption or Hik-Partner Pro cloud API access. The HTTPS API cannot be entered as an ADM-CID TCP receiving center.

Direct ISAPI polling needs an actual private network/VPN route from the control plane to the panel. Dashboard connection tests/discovery also need that route. The existing camera edge-agent tunnel does not expose AX PRO ISAPI automatically.

For an ARC-only installation, keep ISAPI polling disabled. Create the integration with the known panel LAN address and register an approved AX_PRO_HUB in device inventory with the correct tenant/branch, metadata.axProIntegrationId and metadata.axProConfig from that integration. Associate peripherals with verified metadata.axProDeviceId zone identities. ISAPI discovery stages this information when private access exists; receiver events alone do not discover inventory.

docs.title: Application changes
docs.text:
• Browser APIs validate the session against the control plane, use its verified tenant and require a super/company/HQ administrator. Cross-site writes and mandatory-password-change accounts are rejected. Creation verifies branch ownership.
  • Database access uses the canonical PostgreSQL pool/TLS policy. Credentials stay in the vault; secret-provider requests use bounded HTTPS in production.
  • HTTP requests negotiate digest without preemptive Basic, support MD5/SHA-256 digest variants, reject redirects and malformed JSON/XML/entity declarations, preserve endpoint query parameters and enforce deadlines through body streaming with a 1 MiB cap. XML zone/event IDs retain leading zeroes.
  • The optional control-plane worker polls up to four panels concurrently, reducing concurrency for small database pools. It respects intervals, retries failures and drains on shutdown. Advisory locks prevent overlapping manual/replica polls.
  • Polling records the approved source device's health. Hub telemetry is not presented as individual telemetry for every peripheral; peripheral health is available through the configured adapter/device-health API.
  • Event rows, counters and polling cursor commit together. Tests/discovery do not advance that cursor; polling overlaps by 30 seconds. Push updates counters without moving it. Daily counters use the database calendar date.
  • Production push requires an integration-specific secret and timestamp within five minutes. Duplicate deliveries are acknowledged without incrementing counters. Stable identities tolerate key ordering and hub re-enrollment.
  • Disarm/restoration/intrusion mappings are corrected. Unknown vendor codes stay INFO events for review. Integrations can be paused/enabled; paused integrations reject polling/push. Connection tests do not enable them.

docs.title: Migrate and configure
docs.text:
Run npm run db:migrate against the intended deployment database before starting this build. New 091_axpro_schema_prerequisites.sql supplies tables before immutable migration 092; migration 146 remains compatible. 20261010_axpro_production_runtime.sql adds runtime columns, P0–P4 severity compatibility and integration-scoped event identity. Existing migration files were not rewritten.

Use deploy/axpro.env.example (see repository root) for settings:

Setting Service Purpose DATABASE_URL and canonical DB TLS/CA settings Dashboard + control plane Shared database AXPRO_SECRET_VAULT_PROVIDER Both HASHICORP_VAULT or HTTP_JSON AXPRO_SECRET_VAULT_ENDPOINT Both HTTPS vault endpoint AXPRO_SECRET_VAULT_TOKEN / namespace Both Private restricted credentials AXPRO_POLLING_ENABLED=true Control plane Enable ISAPI worker after private routing is verified AXPRO_RECEIVER_SECRETS Dashboard Private JSON map: tenant-id:integration-id to a random secret of at least 32 characters

Compose templates now pass these variables. Polling defaults to false. The GCP dashboard matches its control plane's existing private-container DB transport policy; external deployments should configure verified TLS/CA material. Never use NEXT_PUBLIC_ for credentials or receiver secrets.

Vault reference example: secret://branches/<branch-id>#axpro. Its value must contain JSON username and password. HashiCorp KV v2 references must include the correct mount/data path. Trust the panel/enterprise CA in Node when required; do not disable global TLS verification.

docs.title: Setup screens
docs.text:
1. Sign in as an administrator and open /settings/integrations/hikvision/ax-pro.
  2. Enter the actual branch UUID, panel address, HTTPS port and vault reference.
  3. Keep /ISAPI/System/deviceInfo. Configure capabilities, zone, status and event endpoints only after firmware-specific verification; leave unsupported paths empty.
  4. Test, discover, then approve/enroll identified devices in the hub. Verify zone identities against physical sensors.
  5. Use /security-devices/integrations to test, poll, pause or enable.

The optional events endpoint must return a complete bounded batch for the ISO since query, or be a bridge implementing that contract. Native streaming alertStream and vendor-specific paginated searches are not supported by this snapshot polling client. Use receiver push for these workflows. A health-only poll does not advance the event cursor.

docs.title: Receiver export hook
docs.text:
The ARC receiver must durably queue decoded records with stable IDs and verified semantics:

{
  "eventId": "receiver-persisted-event-000001",
  "eventType": "panic",
  "zoneId": "7",
  "dateTime": "2026-10-10T15:30:00+05:30"
}

For Contact ID, decode the event code and qualifier, including alarm versus restoration. Do not map every numeric code to an intrusion/panic. Retain unmapped codes and verify eventTypeMap using real examples.

On the receiver host, privately set AXPRO_FORWARD_BASE_URL=https://<dashboard-domain>, AXPRO_FORWARD_TENANT_ID, AXPRO_FORWARD_INTEGRATION_ID and AXPRO_FORWARD_SECRET matching the dashboard's integration-specific secret. Invoke from its durable delivery workflow:

node scripts/axpro-forward-event.mjs queued-event.json

The script signs and POSTs original file bytes to /api/security-devices/integrations/<id>/events and leaves the file intact. Signature: HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + rawBody). Headers: x-sentinel-tenant-id, x-sentinel-axpro-timestamp (Unix seconds), x-sentinel-axpro-signature (sha256=<hex>).

202 means a committed event or durable duplicate recognition. Retain/retry on timeout or non-202 with a fresh timestamp/signature. The upstream receiver owns the durable queue and native protocol ACK; this script is the HTTPS forwarding hook, not an ARC listener.

docs.text:

docs.title: Verification and rollout
docs.text:
npm test -- test/axpro.test.ts test/axpro-api.test.ts test/axpro-forwarder.test.ts test/security-device-discovery.test.ts
npm run typecheck
npm run dashboard:typecheck
node scripts/test-axpro-migrations.mjs

The migration test uses a disposable PostgreSQL 17 Docker container without host ports or persistent volumes and does not read a production DB URL. It checks fresh ordering, replay, P1 severity, deduplication, cursor columns and locks. Unit/API tests exercise digest, body limits/deadlines, malformed input, signing, authorization, disabled integrations, transaction rollback, duplicate counters, cursor isolation and recovery. Forwarding tests verify exact-byte signatures and preserve queued files on rejection/timeout.

Before branch activation, test native ARC communication, alarm/restore, arm/disarm, tamper/restore, power-loss/restore, battery/fault and communication-loss supervision. Verify tenant, branch and zone. Replay an event, disconnect/reconnect delivery and verify queue recovery, then test wrong secrets/timestamps and pause/re-enable. Confirm the desired control-room/notification workflow consumes these security-device events; storing them alone does not guarantee SMS/email.

Receiver deployment/export wiring, private reachability, hardware acceptance and production rollout remain outstanding. To stop the integration, pause it and disable the polling worker; preserve receiver queues. The additive schema can remain during application rollback.

docs.title: Database entities and migrations
docs.text: The control-plane migration runner excludes guardian-network-schema.sql, a standalone schema for a separate Guardian Network service. It stops on failed or duplicate-object migrations and rolls back without recording them as applied. Installations upgraded from the older runner must inspect any formerly skipped migration and reconcile actual schema objects before release.

docs.title: Database technology
docs.text:
The control plane uses PostgreSQL through the pg package and a shared pool. The initial schema uses UUID keys, pgcrypto, and PostgreSQL ltree for hierarchical resource paths. Docker definitions supply PostgreSQL 16 or 17 depending on the selected Compose file. Redis is separately configured for runtime state/event use; it is not a replacement for the PostgreSQL schema.

The migration inventory is maintained in database/migrations/ rather than a fixed count in this document. The runner also checks a legacy backend/database/migrations/ directory when present; no files were present there in this checkout.

docs.title: Migration behavior
docs.text:
scripts/run-migrations.mjs:

  1. Reads .sql filenames from the root migration directory and optional legacy directory, deduplicates by filename, and sorts with numeric-aware filename ordering.
  2. Connects using DATABASE_URL and takes a PostgreSQL advisory lock.
  3. Creates schema_migrations with filename, execution timestamp, SHA-256 checksum, and elapsed time.
  4. Can baseline selected portions of an existing core schema when the table is empty and recognizable schema objects already exist.
  5. Applies each pending SQL file inside a transaction and records its checksum.
  6. Reports applied, pending, and database-recorded migrations with no matching file using npm run migrate:status.

Checksum validation is enabled by default. An intentional legacy reconciliation may use SKIP_MIGRATION_CHECKSUM_VALIDATION=true; review actual schema and retain the reconciliation record before doing so. Once a migration has shipped, add a new migration rather than editing the old SQL.

Any SQL failure, including an “already exists” error, rolls back and stops the runner. Failed work is never recorded as an applied migration. Guardian Network's standalone schema is excluded from control-plane migrations.

The Docker entrypoint runs the migration runner before starting the compiled control plane. In Compose, PostgreSQL's /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d mount is also present; PostgreSQL only runs that mechanism on initialization of an empty data directory. Do not confuse that one-time image behavior with the application's repeatable migration runner.

docs.title: Migration domains and source of truth
docs.text:
The migration series begins with core tenant/resource/camera/user/access tables, then grows through authentication, camera grants, recording, analytics, evidence, incidents, compliance, maintenance, privacy, operations, edge lifecycle, storage/recovery, signed configuration, HA/DR, communications, and date-stamped product updates. Files include both additive schema changes and data/configuration changes; inspect each SQL file before applying it.

The canonical complete migration inventory and exact DDL are the files in database/migrations/. There are duplicate numeric prefixes and date-prefixed files, so use the runner's actual sorted order rather than inferring order from a numeric prefix.

docs.title: Safe schema operations
docs.text:
• Snapshot and verify the target database before any production migration.
  • Test migrations against a disposable database using npm run migrate:test where its prerequisites are available.
  • Check npm run migrate:status and deployment logs.
  • Do not edit or reorder migrations already applied to an environment.
  • Run restore and destructive schema exercises only against explicitly identified non-production targets unless the approved recovery plan says otherwise.

For database backup and recovery, see Operations.

docs.text:
npm ci
npm run dev

Set DATABASE_URL and the service settings required by the paths being exercised. The root development command launches only the control plane. Database setup and migrations are described in Getting started.

Workspace commands include:

npm run dashboard:dev
npm run media:dev

The recording engine has workspace-level commands; inspect recording-engine/package.json for the current scripts. The services may need each other's URLs and shared keys to exercise integrated behavior.

Root scripts in package.json include:

npm run build
npm run typecheck
npm run typecheck:all
npm test

typecheck:all includes root and configured workspaces; build:all also attempts the edge executable build. Some scripts require local services, native/runtime assets, cloud access, Windows packaging, or specific environment values. Run focused selectors first and record prerequisites and failures.

Additional script families cover storage, TLS, cameras/recorders, HA, evidence, alerts, telemetry, scale, and chaos testing. See package.json for the current script list rather than relying on this summary as an exhaustive command index.

docs.title: Change workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify the owning service, route, repository, schema, and dashboard surface.
  2. Trace authorization and tenant/resource scope for both reads and writes.
  3. Add a forward-only SQL migration when persistence changes; never rewrite an already deployed migration.
  4. Update tests, route contracts, and the OpenAPI file when API behavior changes.
  5. Run focused tests and typechecks for every affected workspace.
  6. Run build/release checks appropriate to the target artifact.
  7. Document configuration, operational effects, migration requirements, and known limitations.

docs.title: API and data conventions
docs.text:
Fastify control-plane routes are registered in the control-plane app. Services also expose their own routes. The checked-in OpenAPI document is partial and is not generated from every route; update and validate it deliberately when a documented API changes.

PostgreSQL schema changes are under database/migrations/. Migration runs are serialized and recorded in schema_migrations. Review the runner's checksum setting before production use; checksum checking is off unless explicitly enabled.

docs.title: Security and logs
docs.text:
• Preserve default-deny authorization and tenant/branch checks.
  • Validate inputs using existing schemas/helpers and add negative tests.
  • Keep shared keys, database URLs, camera credentials, and model access credentials out of source, tests, snapshots, and logs.
  • Do not enable development identity shortcuts in exposed deployments.
  • Keep external service errors visible; do not silently convert failed integrations into success responses.
  • Preserve relevant third-party license and attribution files when changing bundled runtimes.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This guide is for operators and investigators using the dashboard. Menu visibility and available actions depend on assigned permissions, enabled features, service configuration, and the deployment's device inventory.

docs.title: Open the dashboard
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the URL provided by your administrator.
  2. Sign in using the identity method configured for your organization.
  3. Confirm the organization/branch context shown by the application.
  4. Use only authorized branches and devices. If expected data is absent, ask an administrator to check scope, data freshness, and feature configuration.

docs.title: View cameras and video
docs.text:
Use the live/video or operations camera pages to find an authorized camera. Select a camera and request live view when available. Video requires the camera to be reachable, correctly configured, supported by the media path, and authorized for your account. A blank player can indicate a stream, network, browser transport, credential, or permission issue; it does not prove that the camera is physically offline.

The dashboard also contains playback, bookmarks, video search, and synchronized playback pages. Results depend on indexed recordings, retention, permissions, and enabled services.

docs.title: Review alerts and incidents
docs.text: Use alert/command-center and incident pages to review events. Where permitted, the interface may provide acknowledge, assign, escalate, comment, or investigation actions. Follow your organization's response policy and verify that external notifications were delivered when required.

docs.title: Preserve evidence
docs.text: Use the evidence and investigation workflows for approved capture, review, and export. Follow local chain-of-custody, redaction, retention, and legal-hold procedures. Do not download or redistribute footage unless you are authorized.

docs.title: Understand status
docs.text: Health pages can report stale, unavailable, estimated, or unknown readings. Check the observation time and reason/context before interpreting a status. Maintenance or telemetry pages may require an administrator to correct inventory or connectivity.

docs.title: Get help safely
docs.text: Provide support staff with the time range, affected branch/camera identifier, screen/page, and a redacted error message. Do not send passwords, session cookies, tokens, camera credentials, private recordings, or personal data through unapproved channels.

docs.title: Feature inventory and implementation status
docs.text: This inventory groups source-backed capabilities by operational domain. The project contains hundreds of route and migration modules; a checked-in route, page, migration, or package proves repository implementation evidence only. It does not prove that the feature is enabled, supported in a specific deployment, or verified end to end.

docs.title: Present in source
docs.text: Domain Repository evidence Identity and organization Auth routes and middleware; user, role, session, organization, hierarchy, grant, and feature-management schemas/routes. Cameras and edge fleet Camera/device inventory, discovery, provisioning, edge-agent lifecycle, telemetry, and edge configuration route families. Live video and media Live-session and on-demand media routes; separate media gateway; MediaMTX configuration; dashboard live/video pages. Recording and playback Recording engine, recording/search/recovery/playback routes, storage and retention modules, timeline/bookmark and synchronized-playback schema. AI/analytics Analytics engine; analytics, AI search, ANPR, fall, crowd, face, re-identification, violence, obstruction, tamper, abandoned-object, and tailgating route families. Alerts and incidents Alert command center, operations, suppression, notifications, incidents, playbooks, escalation, and event-stream route families. Dashboard Next.js pages for analytics, operations, admin, compliance, maintenance, playback, communications, security devices, reports, and other workspaces.

docs.title: Conditional behavior
docs.text:
The following require deployment or runtime prerequisites:

  • External OIDC/SAML/LDAP providers and notification channels require valid provider configuration and network access.
  • Live/recorded media requires compatible device protocols, working stream credentials/secrets, gateway connectivity, and suitable client transport.
  • Analytics requires supported inputs, rules, feature configuration, and required model artifacts. The Docker entrypoint attempts to fetch an ArcFace model when it is absent.
  • Storage tiers, cloud archive, SMTP notifications, federation, TURN, and managed tunnels need their corresponding external services and secrets.
  • Feature-management code is active, so a registered UI or route alone does not mean a tenant has the feature enabled.
  • The edge agent's Windows release is supplied separately from Git; the control-plane Docker build verifies that release before proceeding.

docs.title: Explicitly incomplete or unsupported behavior
docs.text:
These are specific source-level limitations found during review:

  1. analytics-engine/src/detectors/face-analytics.ts contains a TODO for attribute detection. Face-related routes/schema do not establish that attribute detection is implemented.
  2. edge-agent/src/recorders/adapters/hikvision-recorder.adapter.ts throws for unsupported adapter operations. Do not infer full Hikvision ISAPI coverage from the adapter's existence.
  3. AI Assistant V2 route registration is conditional in the control-plane app; registration can be skipped when its database pool is unavailable or its optional import fails.
  4. The checked-in OpenAPI contract covers only a subset of the route surface and has a declared version that differs from the root package version. It must not be treated as the exhaustive API contract.

This list is not a complete TODO audit. Search source and test the exact feature and adapter operation before making a support commitment.

docs.title: Planned features
docs.text: A proposed VMS competitive improvement plan now records priorities and acceptance targets. It is not an approved delivery commitment. No authoritative approved roadmap or full planned-feature register was found in the reviewed repository. TODOs, disabled rules, dormant routes, feature flags, and future-looking migration names are not labeled as planned here.

docs.title: Release acceptance
docs.text: For each capability, validate the specific package/build, required migrations, feature settings, provider credentials, hardware/model prerequisites, and end-to-end test path. Capture the result for the deployed revision. No production acceptance results are implied by this repository inventory.

docs.title: Installation and local deployment
docs.text: This guide covers the repository's included Compose stack and a control-plane development process. It is not a substitute for a production runbook.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Git.
  • Node.js 22 or later and npm (declared by the root package).
  • Docker Engine and the Docker Compose plugin.
  • A separately supplied Windows edge-agent release and checksum manifest for building the root control-plane image. The Dockerfile verifies this input and intentionally fails when it is missing or mismatched.
  • Deployment-specific secrets and a PostgreSQL connection string.
  • PostgreSQL must have pgvector installed for migration 014_enable_pgvector_faces.sql. The Compose definitions use matching PostgreSQL 16/17 images with pgvector. The supported images are documented by pgvector. These definitions support new installations. Validate backup/restore and collation compatibility before changing the image of an existing database.

docs.title: Configure the Compose stack
docs.text:
The root compose.yaml starts the API, dashboard, media gateway, recording engine, analytics engine, MediaMTX, Redis, and PostgreSQL. It requires these values (do not use real values in source control):

Variable Purpose in Compose DATABASE_URL API PostgreSQL connection string DB_PASSWORD PostgreSQL container password MEDIA_GATEWAY_SHARED_KEY API-to-media service authentication REPORT_DOWNLOAD_SECRET Signed report-download secret EDGE_BRIDGE_SHARED_KEY Edge bridge shared authentication RECORDING_ENGINE_SHARED_KEY API/recording service shared authentication ANALYTICS_ENGINE_SHARED_KEY API/analytics service shared authentication ANALYTICS_SOURCE_SHARED_KEY Analytics source authentication DASHBOARD_DEV_USER_ID Dashboard build/runtime user identity setting

Other optional values and service-specific controls are defined directly in compose.yaml and the service .env.example files. Inspect those definitions before enabling an integration. Use a secret manager or a local untracked environment file; never paste secrets into checked-in files.

The root Compose file publishes several service ports on the Docker host and uses a simple local PostgreSQL configuration. Do not expose it to an untrusted network as-is. For production considerations and the separate docker-compose.production.yml, see Deployment.

docs.title: Start services
docs.text:
After setting required environment values in your shell or a Compose-compatible environment file:

docker compose -f compose.yaml config
docker compose -f compose.yaml up --build -d
docker compose -f compose.yaml ps

The control-plane image entrypoint attempts to download an ArcFace model if the configured model file is missing, runs database migrations, and then starts the API. A failure to download a required model or connect to PostgreSQL prevents successful startup. Model-source access and model integrity are deployment responsibilities; SHA-256 verification occurs only when a checksum is configured.

Check service health using Compose status and the configured /health endpoints. The dashboard is published on port 3000, the control plane on 8080, the media gateway on 8090, the analytics engine on 8092, and MediaMTX ports are published as specified in the Compose file. Do not assume that an open TCP port means the relevant application function is configured.

Stop the stack:

docker compose -f compose.yaml down

Named volumes persist PostgreSQL, Redis, and recording data. down without --volumes does not remove them. Deleting volumes is destructive; take and verify backups first.

docs.title: Run only the control plane in development
docs.text:
npm ci
$env:DATABASE_URL = "postgres://<user>:<password>@<host>:5432/<database>"
npm run migrate
npm run dev

npm run dev starts src/index.ts only. PostgreSQL must be reachable and required application configuration must be set. External services are not automatically started by this command. For service-specific development commands, use the Developer Manual.

docs.title: First-run verification
docs.text:
1. Confirm PostgreSQL is reachable and npm run migrate:status shows the expected migration state.
  2. Confirm each required container is healthy and inspect its logs.
  3. Verify an authorized user can sign in and access only their intended tenant/branch scope.
  4. Test live view, recording, alerts, and device operations only with equipment and credentials authorized for the environment.
  5. Verify backup and restore procedures in a non-production environment.

These checks are operator actions; the repository does not establish that they have been completed for a particular installation.

docs.title: Health and observability
docs.text:
The control plane exposes health/readiness/metrics endpoints in the checked-in OpenAPI contract. The root and production Compose files define service health checks. The production Compose file also includes Prometheus, Alertmanager, and Grafana services with mounted configuration.

Monitor at least:

  • API and dependency readiness;
  • PostgreSQL capacity, connection health, backups, and migration status;
  • Redis availability and persistence configuration;
  • recording volume free space, recording continuity, retention, and integrity checks;
  • edge-agent and camera telemetry freshness;
  • media gateway/MediaMTX reachability and playback failures;
  • analytics model/pipeline health and alert delivery;
  • TLS certificate expiry and external provider failures.

Telemetry values can be stale, estimated, unavailable, or unsupported. Monitor age and quality as well as value. Configure alert receivers and test delivery; the presence of Prometheus rules or notification code does not mean alerts are being delivered.

docs.title: Database backup
docs.text:
The root package provides npm run backup:database, implemented by scripts/backup-postgres.mjs. It runs pg_dump in custom format and writes a sidecar JSON manifest containing a SHA-256 checksum and an encryptedAtRestRequired marker.

npm run backup:database

The script does not encrypt the dump, upload it, enforce retention, or verify a restore. Store dump and manifest in access-controlled encrypted storage; keep keys separate; define retention and deletion policy; and record backup age and completion outside the database being protected.

The database backup does not include recording volumes, Redis data, external object storage, media configuration, model files, secrets, or separately distributed edge releases. Back those up using the relevant storage/platform procedure.

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
The restore helper requires:

  • a .dump file plus matching <dump>.manifest.json;
  • a RESTORE_DATABASE_URL environment variable (it deliberately ignores DATABASE_URL);
  • explicit --confirm-restore;
  • pg_restore available on PATH.

Example invocation after verifying the target, backup, and change approval:

$env:RESTORE_DATABASE_URL = "postgres://<user>:<password>@<host>:5432/<target>"
node scripts\restore-postgres.mjs .\backups\<backup>.dump --confirm-restore

The helper verifies the backup SHA-256 against the manifest and calls pg_restore --clean --if-exists --no-owner. This is destructive to objects in the target database. Restore first into an isolated database; inspect the restored schema/data and application compatibility before any cutover. A successful process exit is not by itself a business-level recovery validation.

docs.title: Recovery checklist
docs.text:
1. Declare the incident and identify affected service, tenant, time range, and data stores.
  2. Isolate or fence the intended recovery target. Confirm it is not the active production database.
  3. Preserve relevant logs and evidence; avoid overwriting the only known-good backup.
  4. Verify the dump checksum and required storage/model/configuration backups.
  5. Restore and validate in isolation.
  6. Reconcile migration status, user access, service connectivity, recordings, evidence metadata, and telemetry.
  7. Follow approved cutover/failback steps and monitor for divergence.
  8. Record outcome, data-loss window, and follow-up actions.

The repository does not set an RPO/RTO or prove that an organization has completed a recovery drill. Define these with service owners and test them.

docs.title: Recording and object storage
docs.text: Recording engine source includes local and additional storage/failover/export code paths. Configure persistent storage with appropriate capacity, permissions, monitoring, backup, and retention. Validate the specific storage backend and failure path; the local Compose volume is not a production backup strategy.

docs.title: Release and rollback
docs.text: The package includes release preflight, production-release, and rollback scripts. Review their safeguards and target configuration before use. Avoid manual rollback of database changes unless the recovery plan explicitly supports it; many migrations are forward changes.

docs.title: 1. Design summary
docs.text:
The system is a multi-process TypeScript application. A Fastify control plane owns HTTP APIs and coordinates identity, authorization, persistence, and operations. A Next.js dashboard provides the web UI. Separate services handle media routing, recording/storage, and analytics. Branch-local edge agents perform local discovery/monitoring and communicate with central services. PostgreSQL is the durable schema store; Redis is present in the supplied container definitions for shared runtime services.

The diagrams show repository-declared service boundaries and intended interactions. They are logical views, not proof that every integration is enabled in a given deployment.

docs.title: 2. Components and responsibilities
docs.text: Component Entry point / source Design responsibility Control plane src/index.ts, src/app.ts Starts telemetry/config, database/store and runtime dependencies; builds Fastify app; registers API areas; starts HTTP/WebSocket service and graceful shutdown. Dashboard dashboard/ Next.js React application for operator and administrative pages; communicates with control-plane and service proxies. Media gateway media-gateway/src/index.ts, media-gateway/src/app.ts Fastify media boundary with control-plane integration, access/session handling, and MediaMTX-facing HLS/WebRTC routes. Recording engine recording-engine/src/index.ts Recording, storage adapters, retention, evidence capture, integrity, and recovery-oriented workflows. Analytics engine analytics-engine/src/index.ts, analytics-engine/src/app.ts Detection/analytics pipeline, model usage, metrics, and incident/alert forwarding. Edge agent edge-agent/src/index.ts Branch-side discovery, device health, media/runtime setup, telemetry/presence, and supported signed-update/configuration paths. PostgreSQL database/migrations/, src/database/ Relational system of record, migration history, and repository-backed access. Redis Compose service and runtime integrations Shared runtime state/event integration where enabled. MediaMTX Compose service/config Media streaming backend configured for HLS/WebRTC transport.

docs.text:
flowchart LR

    Web -->|HTTP / BFF| API[Fastify control plane :8080]
    API --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
    API --> Redis[(Redis)]

    Media --> MTX[MediaMTX]
    MTX --> Cameras[Camera / recorder streams]

Ports shown are the defaults in the root Compose file; production deployments may override ports, addresses, and topology.

docs.title: 4. Runtime startup and readiness
docs.text:
The root control-plane process initializes telemetry and configuration, establishes PostgreSQL and store behavior, initializes Redis-related services, bootstraps modules, creates the Fastify application, binds its listener, initializes WebSocket handling, and registers graceful shutdown. The container entrypoint runs migrations before starting the compiled control plane.

The API has health/readiness routes and the supplied containers define health checks for several services. A health endpoint only reports the component's implemented check; it does not guarantee all integrations are healthy.

docs.title: 5. Request authorization flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant UI as Dashboard
    participant API as Control plane
    participant Auth as Auth/session middleware
    participant Store as PostgreSQL/store
    User->>UI: Submit request
    UI->>API: HTTP request with supported credential
    API->>Auth: Global pre-handler / CSRF checks
    Auth->>Store: Resolve active user and validate session
    Store-->>Auth: User/session state
    Auth->>Store: Evaluate tenant, role, grant, and resource scope
    Store-->>Auth: Authorization result
    alt Authorized
        Auth-->>API: Attach sanitized current user
        API-->>UI: Route response
    else Rejected
        Auth-->>UI: Authentication/authorization error
    end

The middleware accepts bearer/session credentials and cookies; a development header identity path also exists in source. Do not enable development-only identity behavior in a production exposure.

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor Operator
    participant UI as Dashboard
    participant API as Control plane
    participant GW as Media gateway
    participant MTX as MediaMTX
    participant Cam as Camera / recorder
    Operator->>UI: Request live view
    UI->>API: Create live session for camera
    API->>API: Check user, tenant, branch, and camera access
    API-->>UI: Short-lived authorized session response
    UI->>GW: Request authorized media playlist/session
    GW->>MTX: Resolve configured stream and transport
    MTX->>Cam: Open supported camera stream
    Cam-->>MTX: Media packets
    MTX-->>UI: Configured HLS/WebRTC media

The exact endpoint/token exchange and client transport are implemented across service routes and can vary by configuration. This diagram is conceptual; use the service contract and integration tests for exact wire-level details.

    Edge --> CP[Control plane]
    CP -->|persist inventory, access, audit| DB[(PostgreSQL)]

docs.title: 8. Persistence and consistency
docs.text: PostgreSQL SQL migrations define durable entities and schema evolution. The migration runner records filename, checksum, execution duration, and timestamp in schema_migrations; it serializes concurrent migration runs using an advisory lock. Some state is handled by service-local or Redis-backed components; the exact durability depends on the configured service and volume. See Database.

docs.title: 9. Deployment topology
docs.text: The repository contains compose.yaml, a separate docker-compose.production.yml, individual service Dockerfiles, Kubernetes manifests, and platform deployment files. These are alternate deployment artifacts, not a single unified installer. Validate the selected topology, environment, image artifacts, ingress, storage, and operational procedures before deployment.

docs.title: 10. Design constraints and limitations
docs.text:
• Runtime behavior is split across multiple services and requires compatible service URLs/shared keys.
  • The control-plane Docker build requires a separately supplied Windows edge release.
  • Live streaming and analytics depend on device, model, and external service prerequisites.
  • The route modules and OpenAPI contract have different coverage; see API.
  • No repository evidence was found to establish production SLO/SLA values, formal threat-model approval, or recovery objectives.

docs.title: Security operations rollout
docs.text:
Date: 2 October 2026 (Asia/Kolkata).

The Operations landing page links the existing branch health, recording recovery, incident response, failover, banking, AI quality, edge fleet and evidence workflows. These links expose existing modules; they do not establish hardware acceptance.

docs.title: Changes in this increment
docs.text:
• Health observations and quality reports are isolated by tenant and branch.
  • Invalid clocks produce unknown health; delayed replay cannot overwrite newer observations.
  • Recording scans merge overlapping coverage and scope segment/gap lookup to the tenant.
  • The offline outbox supports a disk journal, checksum validation, interrupted-batch recovery, and bounded quota backpressure without evicting in-flight or protected records.
  • Recovery API failures show unknown results and a last-loaded warning, rather than fabricated success.
  • Banking SOP automated checks require a configured probe and evidence IDs before completion. Unconfigured or failed checks stay pending. Automated step dependencies are respected; the engine accepts an injected StepExecutorService for real integrations.

docs.title: Offline journal configuration
docs.text: Set OFFLINE_OUTBOX_JOURNAL_PATH to a dedicated writable file on persistent local storage. Each journal must have a single process owner. Updates write and flush a temporary snapshot before replacement. Storage failures propagate to the caller; they must not be acknowledged as successfully queued. Corrupt journals fail startup. Without this variable the queue remains in memory. This journal is for the src/offline-sync service; the separately implemented edge recording journal and src/edge-product buffer do not automatically use it.

docs.title: Remaining work and acceptance
docs.text:
Area Existing implementation Remaining acceptance or implementation Verified health Scoped observations, freshness and dependency evaluation Durable health projection, vendor probes and UI evidence coverage across every health path Recording assurance Recording gap ledger, retention and edge backfill Scheduled decoded playback probes; verify recovered media rather than catalog metadata alone Incident response Investigation workspace, persistent playbooks and evidence Real sensor/access correlation, operator permissions and end-to-end closure acceptance Safe recovery HA/failover and recording recovery modules Device-specific bounded remediation with post-action probes and rollback Banking workflows BFSI calibration, security policies and banking playbooks Customer-approved rule catalog and real door/duress integrations AI quality Evaluation registry, certification and camera tuning Resolve model artifact integrity failures, then measure real day/night accuracy and false alerts Edge continuity Disk recording journal and optional durable telemetry outbox Deploy persistent volumes; validate restart/reconnect with actual receiver persistence Evidence Signed packages, custody chain and independent verifier Real media export, redaction and signer acceptance in the deployed environment

The broader validation run also found an analytics model checksum mismatch and legacy playbook tests assuming fabricated branch/access responses. A durable playbook test expects labels from an older SOP definition. These failures remain visible; model manifests have not been rewritten to bless unverified artifacts.

Do not claim all eight areas newly implemented, production accepted, or industry-first. No production deployment or real notification/device action was performed by this increment.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Five selected suites passed, 26 tests total: operations reliability, offline edge survivability, recording gap/backfill, AI quality and independent evidence verification. These are local tests with fixtures; they do not prove live model accuracy or delivery. The broader banking and playbook failures described above remain unresolved.

docs.title: Security-relevant implementation
docs.text:
The control-plane app registers Fastify CORS and Helmet, a global CSRF protection hook, authentication/session middleware, and route modules. Authentication middleware accepts bearer/session credentials and cookies, checks active users/session expiry, and updates session activity. A development-header user identity path also exists. Authorization code implements tenant/resource scope checks and default-deny behavior with super-administrator exceptions.

The repository also contains security-related routes, schemas, and packages covering audit, signed edge configuration, device identity, mTLS, OIDC/LDAP, ABAC, HSM/evidence signing, privacy, and feature settings. These code artifacts do not establish that those controls are enabled or correctly configured in a deployment.

docs.title: Configuration and secrets
docs.text:
Configuration is distributed across the root/service .env.example files, Compose definitions, and service config modules. Review the exact selected deployment file to identify required values. Common secret categories include:

  • PostgreSQL and Redis credentials;
  • JWT/session/cookie secrets;
  • API-to-service shared keys for media, edge, recording, and analytics;
  • report download and device enrollment/signing secrets;
  • cloud storage/KMS/model access credentials;
  • SMTP/SMS, OIDC/SAML, LDAP, federation, TURN, and tunnel credentials.

Use a secret manager or a protected deployment environment. Generate independent, high-entropy secrets for each environment and rotate them using the service's supported process. Do not reuse sample values or expose secrets in logs, Compose output, CI artifacts, screenshots, shell history, or support tickets. The checked-in environment examples are templates and must be reviewed before use.

docs.title: Network and transport
docs.text:
• Put public HTTP entry points behind an approved TLS-terminating ingress or reverse proxy; restrict direct service ports to trusted networks.
  • Review CORS allowlists and do not enable broad origins for production.
  • Follow the production Compose settings for database TLS and CA validation where applicable; verify the effective configuration and certificate chain.
  • Restrict PostgreSQL, Redis, MediaMTX, service ports, and metrics endpoints to trusted network segments.
  • Configure TURN/TLS and allowed media paths for communication features that require them.
  • Do not trust localhost or container-internal names as public service addresses.

The root development Compose file publishes several ports broadly and does not provide a complete public-ingress security boundary.

docs.title: Authentication and authorization operations
docs.text:
• Use session-backed production authentication and supported identity-provider configuration; do not use development-header identity in production.
  • Enable CSRF defenses and configure trusted origins for browser workflows.
  • Review tenant and branch/resource grants with a least-privilege test account.
  • Revoke user/device credentials and sessions when access is no longer needed.
  • Review audit records for privileged changes and investigate unexpected authentication/authorization events.
  • Confirm sensitive camera/biometric/recording permissions with privacy and legal stakeholders.

Exact provider flows, password/MFA policies, credential rotation, and organization-specific role assignments require deployment verification.

docs.title: Data protection and evidence
docs.text:
Database backups contain personal, operational, and possibly credential-related data. Encrypt them at rest and in transit, strictly limit access, establish retention and secure deletion, and test recovery. The backup script writes a SHA-256 manifest and marks encryption as required in metadata; it does not encrypt the dump itself.

Evidence hashes, manifests, signing/HSM integrations, audit trails, and chain-of-custody entities appear in the repository. Their presence alone does not certify evidence authenticity, legal admissibility, or regulatory compliance.

docs.title: Security verification
docs.text:
Use npm run test:security, the TLS tests, release preflight, dependency scanning, and secret scanning where configured. Review the repository workflow definitions and their results for the deployed revision. A passing scan is not a complete threat model or penetration test.

Preserve bundled third-party notices. In particular, review edge-agent/runtime/LICENSE and the bundled FFmpeg LICENSE.txt when redistributing the runtime.

docs.title: Connect branches to an existing VPN agent
docs.text:
Open Administration → Shared edge agents (/admin/edge-agent-branches), or use Connect branches to an existing agent on branch onboarding.

  1. Choose the already installed agent at HO, a regional office, or a zone office.
  2. Choose a branch, region, or zone. Select the branches inside that scope.
  3. Enter each branch's VPN-reachable camera/recorder IP addresses or subnets, separated by commas. Use private IPv4 addresses or CIDRs from /20 through /32. A single IP is stored as /32.
  4. Save the assignment. When the agent is online, select Discover cameras, then open branch onboarding to review devices and supply camera credentials.

One agent keeps its original home branch and serves the selected additional branches. Credentials, discoveries, cameras, recovery, commands, and health telemetry retain the destination branch. Remote scans use only the branch's assigned VPN networks and do not expand into the HO agent's local LAN. The home scan excludes remote branch ranges. Automatic discovery scans one branch per idle iteration, checking operator commands between branches. Region and zone selections save the selected current branches; newly created branches must be assigned separately.

The administrator needs device configuration permission for the agent's home branch, the selected scope, and every selected branch. The installed agent must already be activated with its unique gateway identity. Overlapping routed IP ranges across branches on the same agent are rejected. Branches with cameras on that agent must have their cameras moved before the assignment can be removed. Removing an empty branch cancels its pending scan jobs and branch commands.

docs.title: Rollout
docs.text:
Apply database/migrations/20261003_shared_edge_agent_branches.sql before deploying the updated control plane and dashboard. docs.title: 1. Purpose and status
docs.text: This document reconstructs the implemented system requirements from the repository. It is an as-built specification, not a customer-approved requirements baseline. Requirements marked below describe source-backed capabilities; deployment-dependent behavior and limitations are called out separately.

docs.title: 2. Product scope
docs.text:
The repository implements a hybrid surveillance and operations platform composed of a web dashboard, control-plane API, PostgreSQL persistence, media and recording services, an analytics service, and a separately deployed edge agent. The codebase includes camera/device inventory and health, organization and access scoping, live and recorded media flows, analytics/alerts/incidents, evidence, compliance/privacy, and operational maintenance/reporting domains.

The exact feature set available to an operator depends on the selected build, database migrations, feature configuration, service credentials, models, external providers, and connected device support.

docs.title: 3. Users and external actors
docs.text:
Actor Source-backed interaction Dashboard user Uses the Next.js interface and control-plane-backed workflows. Tenant/organization administrator Manages organization-scoped users, branches, devices, and operational settings where permissions allow. Operator/investigator Uses live, alert, incident, recording, evidence, and investigation workflows where configured. Edge agent Reports branch/device activity and communicates with control-plane and media components. External identity provider OIDC/SAML and LDAP-related code and migrations exist; actual provider configuration is deployment-dependent. Camera/recorder/media source Communicates through supported device adapters/protocols; compatibility varies by model and implemented operation. Operations/platform administrator Deploys services, configures secrets and storage, applies migrations, and monitors health.

Role names and exact permissions are configuration/schema dependent; see Security.

docs.title: 4. Functional requirements inferred from active code
docs.text: ID Requirement area As-built evidence and qualification FR-01 Tenant and organization model Tenant-scoped users and a hierarchical resource-node model exist; SQL migrations and authorization code implement scoped access. FR-02 Authentication and authorization The control plane has request authentication, session checks, role/permission data, and default-deny resource authorization. Exact login methods and enabled providers are deployment-dependent. FR-03 Camera and device inventory Routes, repositories, SQL schema, and dashboard pages cover cameras, device inventory, discovery, recorders, edge agents, and health. Reachability and vendor compatibility are not guaranteed. FR-04 Live media Control-plane live-session operations and a separate media gateway/MediaMTX deployment are present. Valid stream secrets, network paths, and media protocols are prerequisites. FR-05 Recording and playback Recording engine source, storage adapters, recording/evidence schema, playback routes/UI, retention, and recovery-related migrations exist. Actual continuity depends on configured storage and services. FR-06 Video analytics An analytics service and route/schema families cover analytics, detections, alerting, and multiple detection domains. Models, rules, camera inputs, and feature settings determine availability. FR-07 Alerts and incidents Alert command-center, incident, notification, escalation, and operational-event modules are present. External notification delivery requires working provider configuration. FR-08 Evidence and investigations Evidence capture, cases/items/exports, chain-of-custody and investigation routes/schema are present. This does not certify evidentiary admissibility or legal compliance. FR-09 Administration and maintenance Organization, feature-management, maintenance asset/work-order/vendor, reporting, and compliance surfaces exist in source. Permissions and enabled integrations gate operations. FR-10 Edge operations Edge agent package, discovery, telemetry, lifecycle, signed-configuration and update code/schema exist. A release executable is supplied separately from Git. FR-11 Health and observability Health/readiness/metrics and operational health/telemetry domains are implemented. Monitoring backends and alert receivers must be configured. FR-12 Communications Communication-related pages, routes, migrations, and a communications build step exist. Production enrollment, TURN, credentials, and network support are prerequisites.

docs.title: 5. Data requirements
docs.text: PostgreSQL is the durable relational store. The schema is evolved by SQL files under database/migrations/; entities include tenants, organization nodes, users and sessions, cameras and devices, edge agents, analytics, alerts, incidents, recording, evidence, compliance, privacy, maintenance, and operational telemetry. Redis is configured in the supplied Compose deployments for shared runtime state. See Database for relationships and migration semantics.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements and observable constraints
docs.text: ID Requirement / constraint Evidence or limit NFR-01 Runtime Root package declares Node.js >=22; TypeScript targets ES2022 and strict checking is enabled for the root compile. NFR-02 API service Fastify control plane; supplied Compose listens on port 8080. NFR-03 Persistence PostgreSQL is required for the normal control-plane deployment and migration runner. NFR-04 Web client Dashboard is a Next.js application; supplied Compose publishes port 3000. NFR-05 Security controls CORS/Helmet, CSRF hook, session/token checks, scoped authorization, shared service keys, and optional deployment TLS controls appear in code/config. Secure deployment still requires correct configuration. NFR-06 Availability/recovery Health probes, storage recovery/failover code, and backup/restore scripts exist. No repository evidence establishes an SLA, RPO/RTO, or a completed disaster-recovery exercise. NFR-07 Performance/scale Performance and scale test runners exist. Their presence does not establish a measured capacity guarantee; run them against the target release and environment. NFR-08 Accessibility/usability A dashboard exists; no verified accessibility conformance statement or usability acceptance baseline was located.

docs.title: 7. Out of scope / unverified claims
docs.text:
• No complete approved product roadmap or signed customer requirements baseline was located. Therefore no future capability is asserted as “planned.”
  • Third-party identity, email/SMS, cloud object storage, cloud model delivery, TURN, federation, and device integrations require configuration and may incur separate service constraints.
  • Device-specific compatibility, AI detection accuracy, legal compliance, evidentiary admissibility, production readiness, availability, and capacity must be validated independently.
  • The repository does not provide enough evidence to assert that all dashboard pages or route modules are supported, enabled, or acceptance-tested together.

docs.title: 8. Acceptance evidence
docs.text: Use the test commands and release checks in Testing and deployment. Record the exact Git revision, environment, database migration status, external-service configuration, test reports, and operator acceptance for each release. Test-source presence alone is not acceptance evidence.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
The repository uses Vitest for many root and workspace tests and provides specialized TypeScript runners. Useful root commands include:

npm run typecheck
npm run typecheck:all
npm test
npm run test:smoke
npm run test:integration
npm run test:security
npm run test:tls
npm run test:config
npm run test:media:on-demand
npm run release:preflight

For a focused test, run the specific Vitest file or documented npm script for the changed domain. Tests may require PostgreSQL, Redis, external services, model assets, device fixtures, or host-specific runtimes. Record skipped tests and missing prerequisites; do not report them as passed.

The root test suite does not automatically represent all workspace suites. Inspect each workspace's package scripts and CI workflow before release. CI configuration includes separate type/build/test and dependency-scan workflows. Verify status for the exact commit intended for deployment.

Performance, scale, chaos, and acceptance runner presence is not a verified capacity/availability result. Execute with controlled infrastructure and retain the measurements.

docs.title: Root Compose stack
docs.text: compose.yaml builds and runs API, dashboard, media gateway, recording engine, analytics engine, MediaMTX, Redis, and PostgreSQL. It is a convenient integrated stack but its ports and database setup are not a complete hardened public deployment. See Installation.

docs.title: Production Compose file
docs.text:
docker-compose.production.yml defines PostgreSQL 16, password-protected Redis, control plane, dashboard, media gateway, recording engine, analytics engine, and Prometheus/Alertmanager/Grafana. It requires additional secrets and external configuration; review the file and .env.production.example before use. Database TLS settings and certificate values must be supplied and validated. Add an approved TLS ingress/network policy and verify published ports are not reachable from unauthorized networks.

These two Compose files differ in ports, versions, services, and required environment. They are not interchangeable without reviewing those differences. The repository also includes Kubernetes and cloud/platform deployment artifacts; this manual does not certify them.

docs.title: Image build constraints
docs.text:
The root Dockerfile uses Node.js 22 Alpine stages, compiles the root application, builds communications code, and verifies a separately supplied Windows edge-agent release. The Windows executable is not tracked in Git and must match its release manifest. A build that fails this verification is expected until a valid release artifact is supplied.

The production image entrypoint downloads the ArcFace model if missing, runs migrations, and starts the API. Model download access and checksum configuration must be reviewed. Do not assume a successful image build means the model, database, or external dependencies will be available at runtime.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
• Pin the exact source revision and built artifacts.
  • Review secrets/configuration and TLS/network boundaries.
  • Validate database connectivity and migration status; back up before schema changes.
  • Confirm edge release checksum and model availability/integrity.
  • Build and test every target workspace, including focused integration tests.
  • Review dependency and secret scans for the exact revision.
  • Validate health/readiness, dashboard login/scope, media, recording, alerting, backup, and restore in a staging environment.
  • Obtain operator/security/privacy approval for the production cutover.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Checks API exits before listening Check DATABASE_URL, database DNS/network, credentials, database availability, and migration logs. The entrypoint runs migrations before app startup. Migration fails or appears skipped Run npm run migrate:status; review exact migration name/logs; verify PostgreSQL version/extensions and backup. The runner can mark certain already-existing-object errors as applied, so inspect actual schema. Dashboard loads but data is missing Check dashboard-to-control-plane URL, authentication/session, tenant/branch scope, feature settings, and API readiness. Live video unavailable Verify camera reachability and credentials, access grant, media gateway/control-plane keys, MediaMTX URLs, supported stream format, and browser transport/network. Recording missing or stops Check recording engine health, assigned storage path/permissions/free space, camera stream input, shared keys, retention, and segment/continuity health. Analytics/AI unavailable Check analytics engine health, model/rule/configuration, required model files and runtime dependencies, and analytics shared keys. Alerts not delivered Inspect alert policy, recipient resolution, provider credentials/network, and notification attempt history. Stale device status Check telemetry timestamps, edge-agent presence/network, device reachability, and whether the displayed reading is estimated/unavailable. Docker build fails at edge release check Supply the required separately distributed Windows release and matching manifest; do not bypass verification. Database restore refuses to run Confirm dump and sidecar manifest match, RESTORE_DATABASE_URL is set, pg_restore is installed, and --confirm-restore is explicitly supplied.

Capture timestamps and redacted logs when escalating. Never include secrets, tokens, camera credentials, or unredacted recordings in logs or tickets.

docs.title: Competitor evidence and limits
docs.text:
The official VC Tech AI product page describes Smart VMS and related services. The improvement plan uses that description as a provisional feature checklist. No competitor login, installation, quote, performance measurement or client-specific configuration was available. Public claims and repository feature counts cannot establish that either product is better for this customer.

The recommended next engineering milestone is the mobile route correction, followed by a real-device live/playback/outage/notification pilot. Retain an exact revision, reproducible configuration and customer task measurements for each acceptance result.

docs.title: VMS competitive improvement plan
docs.text: Prepared 13 October 2026, Asia/Calcutta. Status: proposed engineering and customer-validation plan; not an approved delivery schedule or release claim.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
Make Sentinel Grid the customer's preferred VMS by improving the daily jobs they perform: watching cameras, finding footage, exporting evidence, identifying failed devices, and handling incidents. Cover every major buying criterion, but deliver changes in order of customer impact and prove each improvement.

The customer named VC Tech's VMS but gave no specific reason for preferring it. VC Tech Smart VMS at VC Tech AI is the working comparison; the exact installed product version, configuration, pricing, and customer experience have not been supplied. Public descriptions are vendor claims, not independently measured performance.

docs.title: Competitor baseline
docs.text:
VC Tech advertises single-to-64-camera grids, timeline playback at 1x/2x/4x, screenshots, automatic recording replenishment after network outages, maker-checker access, hierarchical permissions, and web/Android/iOS access. Adjacent offerings include device and recording health, scheduled reports, industry-specific analytics, cloud/hybrid storage, human monitoring, and maintenance ticketing. Source: official product descriptions, reviewed 13 October 2026.

Compare the licensed VMS package first. Price optional analytics, cloud storage, monitoring staff, and maintenance separately on both sides. A competitor's managed service cannot be matched through interface changes alone.

docs.title: What we have and what still needs proof
docs.text:
Repository evidence and local tests establish implementation, not deployment acceptance. A larger layout selector does not establish more usable live streams.

Buying criterion Sentinel Grid evidence Improvement and acceptance work Priority Live monitoring Fleet wall, branch filtering, tours, main/sub streams, full inventory loading and stream budgets: dashboard/components/live-operations-stage.tsx, dashboard/components/live-stage-model.ts, dashboard/lib/fleet-loading.ts Benchmark 1/4/9/16/36/64 actual video feeds; show loaded, playing, paused and failed counts; preserve layouts; verify reconnect and multi-monitor workflows. Existing 144-tile options are not a measured 144-stream capability. Report unavailable footage honestly. Never infer recording health from a heartbeat alone. Use held-out footage, measure misses and false alerts per camera-day, and check capture-to-alert delay and per-camera inference freshness. Maker-checker parity was not established by this review. P0 Mobile operation Mobile/PWA UI, manifests, services and routes Repair the registered mobile routes described below; test scoped live video, playback, durable actions and network recovery on actual Android/iOS devices. Native application parity is unverified. P0/P1 Device compatibility and installation Edge agent and recorder adapters Publish a model/firmware/operation support matrix with live, playback, disk, retention, PTZ and audio results. Test credential rotation, upgrades and rollback. P1 Reporting and maintenance Operational report templates, schedules, downloadable artifacts and maintenance modules Reconcile inventory counts and permissions; verify downloaded files and recipient delivery; validate fault-to-ticket, vendor assignment, escalation and customer-confirmed closure. OTP closure parity is unverified. P1 Storage, resilience and security Retention, legal hold, storage tiers, recovery, HA and security modules Restore actual recordings and database backups; test disk full, service restarts and failover; verify TLS, credential protection and export expiry; get independent security assurance.
