Support staffing and third-party certifications require business work. P1/P2

P0 blocks acceptance of the affected feature. P1 establishes or improves the core customer experience. P2 differentiates an already dependable product. These priorities are recommendations, not assertions that every listed feature currently fails.

docs.title: Current findings that change the order of work
Mobile route behavior needs correction first
docs.text:
src/routes/mobile-operations.routes.ts marks all seven endpoints noAuth. The authentication hook in src/app.ts returns before normal session checking for that configuration. registerMobileOperationsRoutes is called by the app's extended-feature registration block; successful registration in a particular deployed instance has not been checked here.

The acknowledge, escalate, assign and note handlers return fixed success messages without calling persistent incident operations. Home initializes a healthy one-branch summary and a zero critical-alert count; exceptions are swallowed. Call-branch has a fallback phone number. These are source-confirmed behavioral gaps; deployed exposure and exploitability were not tested.

Required implementation:

  1. Require a valid session and tenant/branch authorization for every route and event subscription, using the canonical authorization path.
  2. Load authoritative scoped health and incidents. Return an explicit unavailable state when data cannot be read; derive critical totals from real records.
  3. Persist actions through the existing incident workflow, validate inputs and assignees, handle conflicts and missing incidents, and record the actor.
  4. Return a branch contact only from configured authorized data. Treat a tel: link as opening the dialer, not a delivered phone call.
  5. Back the event stream with scoped real events, reconnect reconciliation and cleanup; the current handler only writes a connected message.
  6. Verify unauthenticated, wrong-tenant, wrong-branch and forbidden-role requests; test persistence after reload and service restart, store failures, audit failures and simultaneous operators. Inspect reverse-proxy access as well.

An existing MobileOperationsService is not proof that the registered handlers use it correctly. Review its scope, persistence and data sourcing before wiring it.

docs.title: Do not repeat already fixed historical findings
docs.text:
The September customer audit is historical. Current notification worker code rejects failed provider results; the default voice provider fails without a configured transport. The recorder collector returns unavailable evidence on probe failure. Retention UI avoids invented dates/days. Fleet loading batches inventory and AI requests; the stage now includes a fleet wall and excludes P4/P5 operational alerts.

Local regression results are recorded in the accompanying baseline report. Actual provider, camera, recording and browser behavior still require acceptance.

docs.title: AI deployment evidence needs a fresh check
docs.text: The 8 October presentation report documented stale branch collectors and degraded fire/smoke analytics at that time. It also distinguished training-frame replays from new live validation. Those observations are historical, not a claim about today's services. Recheck fresh branch frames, collector continuity, model health and real operator delivery before demonstrations. A classifier's confidence score is not a product accuracy measurement.

docs.title: Measurable release targets
docs.text:
These are proposed targets to establish in a controlled pilot. No current result or competitor result is implied. Adjust them using the customer's actual hardware, bandwidth, workflow and detection risk.

Measure Proposed acceptance target How to measure Single-camera startup p95 first fresh decoded frame within 3 seconds on the agreed LAN, 5 seconds on the agreed WAN At least 100 cold/warm starts per profile, measured from operator click, including session setup. Record failures; do not measure only successful starts. 64-camera wall Every eligible tile plays at the declared substream profile for a 60-minute run; no unexplained stalls over 10 seconds Fix workstation/GPU/browser, codec, resolution, FPS, bitrate and network; measure actual decoded FPS, startup, stalls, CPU/GPU/memory and bandwidth. Test each smaller layout separately. Investigation efficiency At least 90% task completion and 20% lower median time than the compared VMS Five operators complete the same find/seek/export tasks, alternating product order. Also compare failure rate, steps and usability feedback. Recording completeness No unexplained loss in a 72-hour controlled recording trial; every known gap visible Reconcile segment manifests, timestamps and independent decoded samples. Verify exported footage, not only index rows. Outage recovery Recover all footage that genuinely exists in the edge buffer after a 30-minute WAN interruption Reconcile hashes, time coverage and playback; restart during recovery; enforce configured bandwidth limits. Specify buffer capacity. Surface permanently unrecoverable intervals. Health freshness Missing telemetry changes to stale/unknown by the configured threshold plus one polling interval Interrupt telemetry and streams independently; test recorder-only, camera-only and WAN failures. Keep recording and reachability evidence separate. Critical alerts p95 committed-event-to-operator-popup within 5 seconds under agreed load; zero silent loss in the controlled sample Reconcile unique event IDs through persistence, queue, browser and receipts. Separately measure capture-to-detection and detection-to-commit latency. AI usefulness Per-use-case precision/recall, false alerts per camera-day and delay meet written customer thresholds Held-out real-site day/night/occlusion samples with ground truth; separate tuning cameras from evaluation cameras; report sample sizes and uncertainty. Mobile actions Authorized actions persist and survive reload; every forbidden access test denied Android/iOS devices, network loss/reconnect, duplicate submissions, session expiry, cross-tenant IDs, scope revocation and backend outage. Reports Exact authorized inventory/count reconciliation; no undisclosed omissions Compare source inventory and generated CSV/XLSX/PDF; check timezones, filters, expiry and actual scheduled delivery. Recovery and availability Define RPO/RTO and trial a 99.9% availability objective before offering an SLA Restore a backup into an isolated environment; simulate component failures; measure sustained service availability. Define included services and exclusions. Installation and support Repeatable pilot onboarding, tested rollback and measured response times Record elapsed engineer time and customer effort; exercise support handoff and after-hours response using agreed staffing.

docs.title: Delivery sequence
docs.text:
Time windows below are planning horizons, not estimates of committed completion. Assign actual people and effort after reproducing the baseline. Hardware access, model evaluation, security review and staffing are dependencies.

Horizon Deliverables Responsible role Exit gate First week Reproduce client tasks, pin both versions, correct mobile authentication/action/data gaps, refresh live health evidence, agree scorecard and test environment Product lead, backend/security engineer, QA Scoped mobile regression tests pass; no fabricated success in reviewed paths; baseline captured Weeks 2-4 Resolve live/startup/stall and playback/export defects found in the pilot; validate recorder models, WAN recovery, reports and real notification receipts Media/edge engineer, backend engineer, QA/operator Core workflow and failure-injection gates pass on representative real devices Weeks 5-8 Simplify core workflows, complete mobile/PWA acceptance, validate approval/ticket workflows, evaluate three priority AI use cases Frontend/mobile engineer, ML engineer, product/operator Operator comparison and held-out AI targets pass; mobile changes persist and recover Weeks 9-12 Scale and soak testing, restore/failover drills, security review, cost/support package and customer comparison demo Platform/security engineer, QA, commercial/support lead Defined capacity tier passes; risks disclosed; customer accepts measured results

Reuse current modules before adding new pages or parallel services. Keep a single authoritative incident, notification, health and recording workflow. Fix causes demonstrated by evidence rather than adding counters or success labels that hide failures.

docs.title: Fair customer comparison and scoring
docs.text:
Run both products against the same authorized cameras, recording periods, operators, workstation and network constraints. Capture license tier, product version and enabled add-ons. Use identical labelled scenarios for AI. If competitor access is unavailable, mark its outcome unknown; do not declare a win from a website checklist.

Category Initial weight Sentinel result VC Tech result Recording integrity and outage recovery 20% Pending real pilot Unknown Live monitoring and performance 15% Pending real pilot Unknown Playback, investigation and export 15% Pending real pilot Unknown Health and alert reliability 15% Pending real pilot Unknown Access control and audit 10% Source gaps identified; acceptance pending Unknown AI quality for selected use cases 10% Pending held-out evaluation Unknown Operator and mobile usability 5% Acceptance pending Unknown Device onboarding and compatibility 5% Acceptance pending Unknown Reporting, support and total cost 5% Acceptance pending Unknown

Weights sum to 100% and should be agreed with the customer. Score each measured category 0-5: 0 fails the required workflow, 1 requires major workarounds, 2 is partial, 3 meets the agreed requirement, 4 exceeds it in a measured way, 5 is a reproducible material improvement accepted by operators. An unknown result is not zero and must not be included in a claimed overall win. Weighted score is sum(weight_percent * score / 5).

Regardless of total score, unauthorized access, falsely completed incident actions, unreported missing footage and silently lost critical alerts block acceptance. Aim first to pass every required category, then outperform on the customer's highest-value tasks. An overall win does not prove superiority in every individual category.

Compare three-year cost at the same branch/camera counts, retention policy and service levels: licenses, AI, infrastructure, storage/egress, deployment, maintenance, operator staffing and support. No competitor price advantage is claimed because no quote was provided.

docs.title: Evidence to retain for every release
docs.text:
Record test ID, exact revision/artifact, operator, device model/firmware, workload, configuration, expected result, actual result, failure count and artifact link. Keep redacted logs, fresh-frame timestamps, recording checksums, permission results, real provider receipts and operator task measurements. Track open defects with owner, priority, acceptance criterion and rollback plan.

The first useful customer demonstration is a completed loop: induce a real camera fault, identify it with its timestamp, create a ticket, restore service, confirm recovery, retrieve an incident's footage and export verifiable evidence. Show both successful and unavailable states. Make a stronger product claim only after the same workflow is measured against the client's VMS.

docs.text: Updated 14 October 2026. Verification began on 13 October; evidence filenames retain that session date. This records local engineering work after the initial competitive baseline. It does not certify a deployed release, error-free operation or a market ranking.

docs.title: Implemented
docs.text: Area Change and verification boundary Mobile incident handling Authentication, active-user checks, tenant/branch scope, read-only restrictions, persistent actions and audit, conflict detection, configured contacts and bounded scoped reconciliation. Unavailable health and actions surface errors. Mobile proxy strips spoofed identities and enforces same-origin cookie mutations. Tests include HTTP stream disconnect. Mobile interface Replaced the separate simulated SOC view with the shared command center. Removed fabricated patrol checkpoints and success messages. Unconfigured SOS/check-in actions are disabled. No field-device acceptance has been performed. Authorization and sessions Administrator privilege derives from explicit roles; usernames, magic IDs and stale flags no longer grant it. Inactive users are denied. Bootstrap access-session expiry matches the one-hour token lifetime. Playback model Recording indexes must be supplied and validated. Missing recordings/keyframes remain unavailable. Partial camera gaps preserve available tracks; seeking back to footage restores the stream URL. Frame-step requests resolve through the index. This does not prove decoded-frame accuracy or connect the standalone model to a recording engine. Evidence model Removed manufactured sealed exports, hashes and related-camera/event data. Clip exports require an injected exporter and validate returned identity, time window, cameras, duration and manifest hash. Integration and byte-level evidence verification remain necessary. SQL operational APIs Health snapshots persist explicit branch identity and metrics; legacy snapshots are backfilled by additive migrations. Health listing aggregates are valid SQL, with latest snapshots and actual issue/correlation rows. ANPR and watchlist mutations return consistent camel-case fields while retaining legacy SQL keys. Detections/violations receive timestamps. Latest watchlist detection fields come from one row. Read-only/inactive users and foreign-tenant branches are rejected in the tested creation paths. Alert truth Watchlist detections no longer report that a blacklist alert was created when integration is unconfigured. Alert generation/delivery remains an open requirement. Storage truth Removed invented 15% free-space headroom for full disks. Critical and warning capacity thresholds now affect operational status and generate the corresponding alert reason. Tests preserve actual zero free space and check near-full severity separately from SMART, RAID and write evidence. Recorder overwrite behavior still needs device acceptance. Analytics lifecycle Core routes load before model initialization and plugin timers. Disabled face recognition avoids unnecessary module loading. Shutdown waits for startup, shares statistics initialization between engines and closes the pool after the last owner; query-failure cleanup releases checked-out clients. Adapter tests use controlled empty model directories and explicit detections, not installed model accuracy as an implicit dependency. Migration safety A failed migration rolls back and is never marked applied. Checksums are validated by default. Guardian Network's separate schema is excluded. All 205 control-plane migrations succeeded on a fresh isolated PostgreSQL database; a second run validated checksums and reported nothing pending. Dependencies and builds Applied compatible dependency updates, supplied the offline-player TypeScript configuration and corrected recorder SDK response-type compatibility. Database images include pgvector for the vector extension. Existing installations still require restore/upgrade acceptance before changing images. Secret handling Removed a hardcoded JWT signing value from a scratch probe; it now requires the environment. Improved scan buffering and test-fixture placeholders. Repository scanning is a heuristic, not proof that deployed credentials are safe.

Broader smoke checks Final run: 158 passed, zero failed, one skipped across 18 files, including statistics lifecycle cases. reports/vms-smoke-2026-10-13.json and .log. The skipped test concerns actual deployment capacity. Documentation and tracked-source secret scan Strict MkDocs build passed. Secret scan passed with native exit 0: reports/vms-secret-scan-check-2026-10-13.json. The scan covers tracked source patterns, not deployed credential validity or repository history. Production dependency audit One high, zero critical, zero moderate: reports/vms-security-audit-continued-2026-10-13.json. The security gate correctly exits nonzero.

PowerShell can turn native stderr into an error record during redirection even when assertions pass. The check runner captures stdout/stderr directly and records the native exit code separately; a JSON test count alone is insufficient.

docs.title: Open release blockers
docs.text:
1. The production dependency audit reports the high-severity node-forge certificate-validation advisory with no registry fix available in the refreshed audit. Replace affected validation paths or take a verified upstream fix, then rerun security tests and the audit. No package-wide exemption was added.
  2. A clean full-suite run has not been established. The earlier diagnostic contained 461 failing assertions across 98 active-source files, after excluding temporary copies (3,948 assertions total). That is historical diagnostic evidence, not the current failure count: selected defects and obsolete fixtures have since been corrected. Communications SQL/service contract tests, analytics/collector failures and other remaining suites need triage and verification.
  3. Review organizational grant enforcement across all SQL operational routes, including list filtering and update/detection scope, beyond the tested tenant, inactive-account and read-only checks. Mobile's canonical scope tests do not certify every other API.
  4. Connect and verify actual clip export, blacklist alert generation, emergency workflows and notification delivery. A truthful unavailable state is useful but does not complete the capability.
  5. Run a real-camera pilot: live-view latency, synchronized playback/decoded frame accuracy, recording gaps, WAN outage/backfill, retention, storage failure, recipient delivery, evidence integrity and restart recovery. Run multi-day soak/capacity tests against the approved recorder/camera matrix. The existing smoke case returns a capacity assessment based on actual deployment remains skipped; no measured deployment capacity is certified.
  6. Benchmark representative customer tasks against the exact VC Tech product and deployment. Public feature claims and local test counts cannot establish competitive superiority.
  7. Rotate the formerly hardcoded JWT signing value wherever it was used and revoke associated tokens. Removing it from the scratch file does not remove repository history or invalidate previously signed tokens.

docs.title: Reproduce safely
docs.text:
The QA stack binds PostgreSQL to 127.0.0.1:55432 and Redis to 127.0.0.1:56379. The script generates an ignored .env.vms-qa credential file; it does not use production database credentials. Fresh migration verification creates an additional disposable database inside that QA container.

node scripts/vms-qa-stack.mjs start
node scripts/vms-qa-stack.mjs migrate
node scripts/vms-qa-stack.mjs verify-migrations
node scripts/vms-qa-stack.mjs test test/anpr-logistics.routes.test.ts test/device-health-correlation.routes.test.ts test/nbfc-watchlist.routes.test.ts
node scripts/vms-qa-stack.mjs smoke
node scripts/run-vms-check.mjs regression
node scripts/run-vms-check.mjs root-build
node scripts/run-vms-check.mjs test-types
node scripts/run-vms-check.mjs analytics-types
node scripts/run-vms-check.mjs secret-scan

Production has not been deployed or migrated by this work. Preserve existing customer data and validate upgrades using a restored staging database before release. Release requires passing checks and the pilot evidence above.
